clue.text: It's a bloomer to hold up confectionery as food

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first, holding it up

parts.note: sweets are confectionery, so the word gives sweet
a bloomer is a type of crusty loaf of bread in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone notes that it is a blunder to prop up sweets and call them a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a mistake but is a British loaf. Because this is a down entry, 'to hold up' puts BREAD underneath SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetbread is an edible organ, pancreas or thymus, eaten as a type of offal.

clue.text: Cook insufficiently on top of grill? One has no chance

parts.note: to underdo food is to cook it too little

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, here taken from grill

explanation.surface: A kitchen query about undercooking something under the grill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places UNDERDO above G, the top of 'grill', in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the competitor given little or no chance of winning.

clue.text: Car test I have for good reason

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles, named after the old Ministry of Transport
I have contracts to I've, spelt without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A driver claims to have a sound excuse for putting the car through its inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly vehicle safety test, required for cars over three years old.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the reason behind an action, here a good reason for doing something.

clue.text: Accomplished the discontinuation of extremes of medication

indicators.note: stopping the extremes means cutting off the first and last letters of the word for medication

parts.note: a tablet is a pill, a dose of medication

explanation.surface: A patient becomes skilled at stopping the most extreme doses of their drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilled or competent, as an accomplished person is.

clue.text: Irrelevant one in crowd scene no use after changing

parts.note: an extra is a film actor with a non-speaking part in a crowd

indicators.note: the words no use are rearranged once changed

explanation.surface: A film extra in a crowd scene is pointless and useless after a costume change.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraneous matter is beside the point, so it is irrelevant to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Beef, grouse or carp?

definitions.meaning: to beef is slang for to moan
to carp is to find fault peevishly

explanation.walkthrough: All three look like nouns, meat, a game bird and a fish, but each is also a verb for grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Each word is an informal verb meaning to grumble or express dissatisfaction.

clue.text: The holiday provided comes up with teas, if ordered

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'

indicators.note: the letters of teas are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday promised if tea is served, as long as someone orders it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns IF into FI; 'ordered' rearranges TEAS into ESTA. 'With' and 'if' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festival or holiday, especially a religious one in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: University type to spend recklessly

definitions.meaning: a sportsperson who has represented Oxford or Cambridge against the other
to ... money is old British slang for squandering it

explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a 'Blue' is awarded for competing against the rival university.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue names both an Oxbridge sporting honour-holder and, in slang, to squander cash.

clue.text: Where the plants have a long shelf life?

definitions.text: Where the plants have a long shelf life?

parts.words: Where the plants have a long shelf life?
parts.note: plants living permanently on a sill or ledge outside the house, a jokey take on a shop item's shelf life

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelf life' normally means how long goods keep; here the shelf is a window ledge where flowers live.
explanation.definitionFit: A planter fixed to a window ledge, so the flowers spend their whole life on a shelf.

clue.text: College heads from Oxford, readers in English literature

indicators.note: the heads of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Oxford college heads drawn from readers in English literature.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is a college of Oxford University, so the surface paints an apt scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the constituent colleges of the University of Oxford.

clue.text: Recluse finding existence empty about to give up

indicators.note: the emptied existence goes about, surrounding, the next piece
an emptied word loses its inside, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: to remit is to refrain from or give up, as in remitting a debt

explanation.surface: A hermit finds life empty and is about to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the usual RE, but here it is the container signal; 'to give up' is the sense of remitting a debt or penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, a religious recluse living alone.

clue.text: Possibly tries round the Post Office for a reply

indicators.note: the anagram goes round the abbreviation
possibly signals that tries may be rearranged into some other order

parts.note: PO is the standard abbreviation for Post Office

explanation.surface: Someone may attempt to get round the Post Office to obtain an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' makes RISTE, the anagram of the fodder, which goes round the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp retort, so it is a reply.

clue.text: Spending allowance to be cut in move

indicators.note: cutting the word means dropping its last letter

parts.note: a budget is an amount allowed for spending

explanation.surface: A spending budget is trimmed in a government move.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to shift or move slightly.

clue.text: Give assistance to finish harvesting first in the country

annotationWithheld.why: Give assistance to finish harvesting first in the country (4,1,4): LAND around END (finish) and H (harvesting first) gives LENDHAND; nothing in the clue supplies the A of LEND A HAND
annotationWithheld.clue: Give assistance to finish harvesting first in the country

clue.text: Final statement from the bar

parts.note: the bar is a pub counter rather than the legal profession, and the closing call is the barman's

explanation.walkthrough: 'The bar' suggests barristers and a closing speech in court; it is the pub, where the barman calls time for the last drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British pub the call for final drinks before closing time is the barman's last announcement.

clue.text: Teased with spin, hooked to outfield … well held

indicators.note: hooked on to means the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: deep is the cricket term for the outfield, far from the batsman

indicators.note: spinning the word teased jumbles its letters

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a teasing spin ball hooked to the outfield, and well caught.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket 'the deep' is the area near the boundary; the surface's catch is a red herring, as 'well held' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-seated belief or problem is firmly established, held strongly within.

clue.text: Can pro so engaged, when stumbling, win this?

definitions.text: Can pro so engaged, when stumbling, win this?

indicators.note: the words can pro so engaged trip up and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A doubt whether a professional runner, tripping up, could still win a school sports race.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a pro who stumbles might drop the egg in this race.
explanation.definitionFit: A school sports-day race in which runners carry an egg balanced on a spoon.

clue.text: Unnecessary pointers to society

parts.note: needles on dials and compasses are pointers

explanation.surface: Pointless signposts directed towards society.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not needed, so unnecessary.

clue.text: Twitch after description of some clues unfinished in puzzle

indicators.note: the twitch comes after the shortened word
an unfinished word loses its last letter

parts.note: in a crossword some clues are labelled across, the others down
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone twitches over an unfinished crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword clues are grouped as across or down; trimming gives ACROS, the clue's own self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle in which initial letters of lines spell a word.

clue.text: It's risky showing rage in party (US)

indicators.note: the rage goes inside the party

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
rage means anger

explanation.surface: Losing your temper at an American party is hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerous means involving danger, which is to say risky.

clue.text: Messenger's Greek letter with bent coin

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: a bent coin is twisted, so its letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A courier carrying a Greek token and a bent coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Messenger' stands for 'is' and links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal envoy, an ambassador carrying the Pope's messages.

clue.text: Receptacle actor uses for part

indicators.note: only a part of the phrase actor uses is taken, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A theatre prop an actor uses in a role.
explanation.walkthrough: In botany the torus is the receptacle, the top of a flower stalk bearing the petals.
explanation.definitionFit: Torus is the botanical name for the receptacle of a flower, from which the floral parts grow.

clue.text: What's worn out around the East in layers?

indicators.note: the tiredness goes around the compass point

parts.note: tired describes something worn out
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A question about faded clothing worn in layers around the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered means arranged in rows or levels, one above another.

clue.text: Girl's hat turns up and is found in the plot

definitions.text: turns up and is found in the plot

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A girl's hat appears in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The plot' suggests a story, but it is a garden plot, where worms turn up when digging.
explanation.definitionFit: An annelid is a segmented worm, such as the earthworm, found in garden soil.

clue.text: OT king's a custom, it turned out

indicators.note: it is thrown out of the word for custom

parts.note: a habit is a custom or usual practice

explanation.surface: An Old Testament monarch's practice, as it turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'OT' is Old Testament; the 's means 'is'. Ahab was a king of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahab was a king of Israel in the Old Testament, husband of Jezebel.

clue.text: A plant: available one in South Africa

parts.note: free means available, as a free seat

indicators.note: the one goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A plant obtainable in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a South African flowering plant with fragrant blooms.

clue.text: Moderate entertainment

definitions.meaning: a funfair with rides and stalls

explanation.definitionFit: Fair means middling in quality, and also a travelling show of rides and stalls.

clue.text: The sign changes when you subtract 5

indicators.note: subtracting takes the Roman five away from the word

parts.note: varies means changes
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A mathematical sign changes when five is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sign' suggests a maths symbol; it is a sign of the zodiac. 5 is the Roman numeral V.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Drink one where inn is abroad

indicators.note: abroad means widely scattered, so the letters go everywhere

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink from a foreign place where the inn is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' hints at foreign travel but signals the anagram of I, WHERE and INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhine wine is a white wine from the Rhine valley in Germany.
